title: Affine pushforward and tensor modules commute with the directed limit
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], let $(S_i)$ be an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] over $I$ with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and let $S=\varprojlim_iS_i$. Fix $0\in I$ and write $g_i:S_i\to S_0$ ($i\ge0$) and $g:S\to S_0$ for the projections. Let $\mathcal F_0$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{S_0}$-module [pqf-def-coherent], set $\mathcal A_i=(g_i)_*\mathcal O_{S_i}$, a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{S_0}$-algebra, and let $\mathcal A=\varinjlim_{i\ge0}\mathcal A_i$ be the directed colimit of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{S_0}$-algebras (whose underlying module is the colimit of the $\mathcal A_i$ in $\mathcal O_{S_0}$-modules). Then: (1) $S$ is identified over $S_0$ with the relative spectrum $\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_{S_0}(\mathcal A)$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec], so that $g_*\mathcal O_S\cong\mathcal A$; (2) there are canonical isomorphisms $(g_i)_*g_i^*\mathcal F_0\cong\mathcal F_0\otimes_{\mathcal O_{S_0}}\mathcal A_i$ and $g_*g^*\mathcal F_0\cong\mathcal F_0\otimes_{\mathcal O_{S_0}}\mathcal A$, compatible with the transition maps; (3) under these identifications, $\mathcal F_0\otimes_{\mathcal O_{S_0}}\mathcal A$ with the maps induced by $\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal A$ is the colimit of the directed system $(\mathcal F_0\otimes_{\mathcal O_{S_0}}\mathcal A_i)_{i\ge0}$ in the category of $\mathcal O_{S_0}$-modules.

proof.text: Restrict to the cofinal directed tail. Put A_i equal to the affine pushforward of the structure sheaf. The quasi-coherent algebra colimit node constructs A as their colimit on affine sections. For an affine open U of S_0, the inverse images U_i in S_i and U in S are affine by the relative-spectrum statement, and the affine-limit statement identifies U with the limit of the U_i. The rings of the U_i have colimit A(U) by the algebra-colimit statement, so the Spec-colimit-limit statement identifies U with Spec A(U), compatibly on overlaps. These local identifications glue to identify S over S_0 with the relative spectrum of A; the relative-spectrum statement then identifies g_* O_S with A.

proof.text: For an affine open U of S_0, write A for its ring, B_i for the sections of A_i, and B for the sections of A over U; by (1) and the relative-spectrum statement, B_i and B are the rings of the affine inverse images of U in S_i and S. The affine pullback sections node gives natural isomorphisms from F_0(U) tensor_A B_i to the sections of the pulled-back F_0 over the inverse image of U in S_i, i.e. to ((g_i)_* g_i^* F_0)(U), and likewise from F_0(U) tensor_A B to (g_* g^* F_0)(U). By the quasi-coherent tensor-sections node, F_0(U) tensor_A B_i and F_0(U) tensor_A B are the sections over U of F_0 tensor A_i and F_0 tensor A. These isomorphisms on the affine opens are compatible with restriction between affine opens and with the transition maps by the naturality in the pullback-sections node, so they define isomorphisms of sheaves (a compatible family of isomorphisms on a basis of opens), giving the asserted pushforward-tensor isomorphisms compatible with transition maps.

proof.text: Let (C, c_i) be the colimit of the directed system (F_0 tensor A_i) in O_{S_0}-modules; by the quasi-coherent module colimit node, C is quasi-coherent and C(U) is the directed colimit of the sections (F_0 tensor A_i)(U) for every affine open U. The maps F_0 tensor A_i -> F_0 tensor A induced by A_i -> A induce a map C -> F_0 tensor A. On an affine U, by the tensor-sections node it is the canonical map from the colimit of F_0(U) tensor_A B_i to F_0(U) tensor_A B, where B is the directed colimit of the B_i by the quasi-coherent algebra colimit node; this map is bijective because tensoring the fixed A-module F_0(U) commutes with directed colimits (tensor-colimit node). A map of sheaves bijective on every affine open is an isomorphism, so F_0 tensor A with the maps induced by A_i -> A is the colimit in O_{S_0}-modules. (Applied with F_0 = O_{S_0}, the same argument shows the underlying module of A is the colimit of the A_i in O_{S_0}-modules.)
